# Copilot Instructions — gesinn-it-pub/oojs-ui

## Purpose

This repository is a fork of [wikimedia/oojs-ui](https://github.com/wikimedia/oojs-ui).
It adds a custom OOUI theme named **SemanticCore** alongside the upstream themes.
The fork is maintained as a thin customization layer on top of upstream releases.

---

## Repository structure

The only files added or modified compared to upstream are:

| Path | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `src/themes/semanticcore/` | **new** | SemanticCore theme — see details below |
| `php/themes/SemanticCoreTheme.php` | **new** | PHP theme class |
| `Gruntfile.js` | **modified** | 1-line addition: `semanticcore: 'SemanticCore'` in the `themes` object |
| `package.json` | **modified** | Adds `gesinn-it-ui-base` dependency (custom Less variable base replacing `wikimedia-ui-base`) |

Everything else is unmodified upstream code.

### Patch-based theme architecture

SemanticCore is a **minimal patch** on top of wikimediaui, not a full copy.
`src/themes/semanticcore/theme.less` is the authoritative declaration of what we own:

```less
@import 'common.less';             // our variables (gesinn-it-ui-base)
@import 'elements.less';           // our overrides (~55 changed lines)
@import 'layouts.less';            // managed copy of wikimediaui — no SemanticCore changes¹
@import 'tools.less';              // managed copy of wikimediaui — no SemanticCore changes¹
@import 'widgets.less';            // our overrides (~26 changed lines + compat fix)
@import 'windows.less';            // our overrides (1 changed line)
```

¹ These files cannot use `@import '../wikimediaui/layouts.less'` directly because Less
resolves the nested `@import 'common.less'` inside them relative to the wikimediaui/
directory — which loads wikimediaui/common.less and overrides our gesinn-it-ui-base
variable values. The copies must live in semanticcore/ so that `@import 'common.less'`
resolves to our variables. A drift-detection script guards against them falling behind:
`scripts/check-theme-copies.sh`

Files imported from `../wikimediaui/` receive upstream changes **automatically** on rebase.
Only the 3 maintained files (`elements.less`, `widgets.less`, `windows.less`) plus the
2 managed copies require review during upgrades.

---

## Branch model

```
upstream/master  (wikimedia/oojs-ui — read-only reference remote)
     │
     ├─ v0.46.1 ─── v0.51.x ─── v0.53.x   (upstream tags, mirrored to fork master)
              \
               customizations branch
               └── [1 squashed commit] feat(theme): add SemanticCore theme
                   tag: 0.46.1-1 / 0.51.x-1 / ...
```

- **`master`** mirrors a specific upstream tag exactly — no custom code lives here.
- **`customizations`** branch carries exactly **one squashed commit** on top of the upstream tag.
- **Fork tags** use the pattern `{upstream-version}-{patch}`, e.g. `0.51.2-1`.
  The patch counter increments only when the theme itself changes at the same upstream base.

---

## Build

The theme is built using Grunt. Only two targets are needed for production artifacts:

```bash
npm install
npx grunt build-styling   # produces dist/*-semanticcore.css + image copies
npx grunt build-code      # produces dist/oojs-ui-semanticcore.js
```

The `demos` target requires Composer and is not part of the production build.

Produced dist files relevant for deployment:
- `dist/oojs-ui-core-semanticcore.css`
- `dist/oojs-ui-images-semanticcore.css`
- `dist/oojs-ui-toolbars-semanticcore.css`
- `dist/oojs-ui-widgets-semanticcore.css`
- `dist/oojs-ui-windows-semanticcore.css`
- `dist/oojs-ui-semanticcore.js` (+ `.js.map.json`)
- `dist/themes/semanticcore/images/` (icons and indicators)

## MediaWiki / OOUI version compatibility matrix

MediaWiki bundles a specific OOUI version. The fork tag used in a MediaWiki installation
**must** be compatible with the OOUI version bundled by that MW release.
The SemanticCore CSS must cover all widget classes generated by that OOUI version.

| MediaWiki | OOUI bundled | Minimum fork tag | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| 1.35.x    | v0.39.3     | `0.44.x-1` ¹     | Fork is intentionally ahead; no known issues |
| 1.39.x    | v0.44.3     | `0.44.x-1`       | Fork was initially developed against this era |
| 1.43.x    | v0.51.2     | `0.51.x-1`       | ⚠ Upgrade required — fork at 0.46.1-1 is behind |

¹ Tested; no CSS class regressions observed in practice. The risk for "fork is ahead"
is lower than "fork is behind" because new CSS simply adds coverage without breaking existing.

**Rule of thumb:** keep the fork tag at or above the OOUI version bundled by the
oldest MediaWiki installation in use.

---

## Upgrade workflow (rebasing onto a new upstream tag)

Run these steps when upgrading to a new upstream OOUI release:

### 1. Pre-flight: assess the diff

```bash
git fetch upstream

# Check for changes to files we touch
git diff v{old}..v{new} -- Gruntfile.js build/modules.js

# Check for variable changes in the base theme (our common.less imports the same vars)
git diff v{old}..v{new} -- src/themes/wikimediaui/common.less

# Check for new .less files added to wikimediaui (= potential coverage gaps in semanticcore)
git diff v{old}..v{new} --name-status -- src/themes/wikimediaui/ | grep "^A.*\.less"

# Check if upstream bumped wikimedia-ui-base or switched to codex-design-tokens
git diff v{old}..v{new} -- package.json | grep -E "wikimedia-ui-base|codex-design-tokens"
```

### 2. Rebase

```bash
git checkout customizations
git rebase v{new}
# Expected conflicts: Gruntfile.js (re-apply 1-line addition) and package.json (re-apply gesinn-it-ui-base)
```

### 3. Check managed copies for drift

```bash
bash scripts/check-theme-copies.sh
```

If drift is reported: copy the upstream file over the semanticcore copy and restore
the header comment block (see the file for the template). Then re-run to confirm.

### 4. Build gate — mandatory before tagging

```bash
npm install
npx grunt build-styling build-code 2>&1 | grep -E "error|Error|Done"
```

A Less compilation error here means a variable was renamed or removed upstream.
Inspect the error, find the variable in `src/themes/wikimediaui/common.less`, and
update `src/themes/semanticcore/common.less` accordingly.

### 5. Tag and push

```bash
git tag {new-version}-1
git push origin customizations --tags
```

---

## What SemanticCore actually changes vs. wikimediaui

The theme is a minimal patch on top of wikimediaui.
`layouts.less` and `tools.less` are not maintained in semanticcore — they are imported
directly from wikimediaui in `theme.less`. All real customizations are confined to:

### Variable layer — `gesinn-it-ui-base` (replaces `wikimedia-ui-base`)

| Variable | wikimedia-ui-base | gesinn-it-ui-base | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@wmui-color-accent30` | `#2a4b8d` (Wikimedia blue) | `#2b566a` (teal-blue) | Hover/active link color |
| `@wmui-color-accent50` | `#36c` (Wikimedia blue) | `#39718b` (teal-blue) | Primary color — buttons, links, focus rings |
| `@wmui-color-accent50--lighten` | `#447ff5` | `#2b566a` | Lighten variant of primary |
| `@border-radius-base` | `2px` | `0.19rem` | All button/input corner radii |

### `common.less` additions

| Variable | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `@size-anchor` | `9px` | Popup widget arrow size (extra, not in wikimediaui) |
| `@background-color-backdrop-light` | *(not defined — wikimediaui defines it as `rgba(255,255,255,0.65)`)* | Falls back to hardcoded `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)` in `windows.less` |

### `elements.less` — button styling

- **`font-weight: bold` removed** from label elements — all input labels render at normal weight.
- **Default framed buttons** use primary color (`@color-primary`) for background/border instead of
  wikimediaui's neutral grey (`@background-color-framed` / `@border-color-base`).
  This makes all unflagged framed buttons visually primary-colored.
- **Icon/indicator invert filter** added for active state: icons on colored button backgrounds
  are forced white via `filter: brightness(0) invert(1)`.
- **Progressive/Destructive flags** use `mw-framed-primary-button-colored` (filled) instead
  of `mw-framed-button-colored` (outline-style), so they render as solid color buttons
  regardless of the `primary` flag.

### `widgets.less` — dropdown & TagMultiselect

- **DropdownWidget menu** gets `margin-top/bottom: -1px` and
  `border-radius: 0 0 @border-radius-base @border-radius-base` — creates a seamless visual
  join between the handle and the open menu.
- **TagMultiselectWidget compat** (added 0.46.1-2): extra `> .oo-ui-tagMultiselectWidget-content > input`
  selector covers the old DOM structure from OOUI < v0.41.2 (MW ≤ 1.35).

### `windows.less` — modal backdrop

- Backdrop overlay hardcoded to `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)` (lighter than wikimediaui's 0.65).

---

### Upgrade impact of these customizations

When rebasing onto a new upstream tag, only `elements.less` and `widgets.less` carry a
meaningful diff risk. The changes are all **semantic** (color logic / structural), not
just variable substitutions, so they must be reviewed manually if upstream changes the
surrounding Less structure. `layouts.less`, `tools.less`, and `windows.less` are safe to
auto-accept upstream changes.

---

## Key dependency: `gesinn-it-ui-base`

`src/themes/semanticcore/common.less` imports from `gesinn-it-ui-base/wikimedia-ui-base.less`
instead of the upstream `wikimedia-ui-base` package.

```less
@import ( reference ) '../../../node_modules/gesinn-it-ui-base/wikimedia-ui-base.less';
```

**Starting with upstream v0.51.x**, `wikimedia-ui-base` was replaced by
`@wikimedia/codex-design-tokens`. Before upgrading to any upstream version that
drops `wikimedia-ui-base`, verify that `gesinn-it-ui-base` provides the required
Less variables, or update `common.less` to import from codex-design-tokens instead.

---

## Gap detection checklist

When upgrading, check these potential gaps manually after the build succeeds:

1. **New Less files in wikimediaui** — new files = new widget families. Check whether
   semanticcore needs equivalent rules.
   ```bash
   git diff v{old}..v{new} --name-status -- src/themes/wikimediaui/ | grep "^A.*\.less"
   ```

2. **New icon JSON manifests** — new icons in wikimediaui have no SVG in semanticcore
   and will fall back to wikimediaui images or be invisible.
   ```bash
   git diff v{old}..v{new} --name-status -- src/themes/wikimediaui/ | grep "^A.*icons.*\.json"
   ```

3. **CSS class renames in OOUI core** — rare but possible. If a widget's HTML class
   changes between versions, semanticcore CSS targeting it silently stops applying.
   Cross-check with `History.md` entries mentioning "rename" or "class".

4. **Visual smoke test** — after deploying the new tag, open a MediaWiki page with
   forms, dialogs, toolbars, and dropdown widgets and verify styling is correct.

---

## Tagging and release convention

- Tag format: `{upstream-semver}-{N}` where N starts at 1, e.g. `0.51.2-1`
- Increment N (e.g. `0.51.2-2`) when theme-only changes are made without an upstream bump
- Commit message for the squashed customizations commit: `feat(theme): add SemanticCore theme`
- Version bump commits (if any) follow: `prepared x.y.z-N [skip ci]`
